answer: Each bonded identity locks collateral in escrow, and equivocation by k coordinated identities incurs a correlated penalty proportional to k², not merely k separate fines. Splitting control among aliases therefore cannot dilute exposure: detection applies an exponential multiplier to aggregate capital loss as the swarm grows, while asymmetric depreciation limits recovery of slashed bonds. The resulting cost ridge discourages a sybil spiral; even a sable adversary cannot evade penalties when shared-control evidence links identities.
